profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer, Microsoft
profile.summary:
I have been involved in software development since 1984. My experience is varied in many dimensions. I have worked in government, telecommunications, financial, and computer hardware industries. I've bit-twiddled in device drivers, used 4th generation languages for expert system development, built models/simulations, updated embedded systems, developed compilers, and designed databases.

I am especially interested in the process of system development.

Specialties: Software development processes
Software development

Background image credit: Eldan Goldenberg. https://www.flickr.com/photos/eldan/8801759560/  Licensed under Creative Commons ShareAlike 4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/)

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: After Microsoft acquired BlueStripe Software, I have continued design and development activities for data collection on supported systems.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: I was an engineer on the Collector development team. In this role, I designed and implemented the subsystems run on the systems being monitored with Factfinder™. The Collector was available on Windows, Linux, Solaris, AIX. Data is collected from kernel and user space instrumentation.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
I was the feature lead for the health and alerting subsystems of the VNXe product line. I was responsible for the overall design of our team's subsystems. I have been the Scrum Master for our eight member team.

Previously, I was a member of the Graphical User Interface (GUI) development team for the Celerra and VNX Network Attached Storage (NAS) product lines. I developed components for Celerra Manager and Unisphere using Java and Struts. I developed a framework for implementing Command Line Interface components using a shared data model with the GUI. I initiated multiple efforts to improve team processes including standardizing design and code review practices, introducing JUnit testing, and using historical defect data to predict software release readiness. I created the team's best practices for customer and Testing reported defect forensic analysis.

I mentored and trained most new team members. This included training sessions, one-on-one coaching using pair programming, doing hundreds of code reviews. The team members were in India, China, and on site.

The GUI development team was part of the larger product development organization. The other teams were located worldwide. Feature development and support activities were always multi-site efforts.

positions.title: Senior Engineer & Founder
positions.description: Prepared the High Level Design for File System components of a new product line of Network Attached Storage (NAS) system. Contributed to the system architecture and the design of other major subsystems and features.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: See individual project descriptions.

positions.title: Consultant Engineer
positions.description: Provided second and third tier support and participated in development for several major kernel components, specializing in the File System, Network File System, TCP/IP, Virtual Disk, Distributed Lock Manager, and Clusters subsystems, as well as enhanced SAN and NAS support. Delivered subsystem specific training, hands-on kernel coding and debugging, design/re-design services, and system documentation mentoring to the junior engineering staff.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: During this engagement, a Keane team provided system enhancements and technology upgrades to a system used by two of the state’s professional regulatory boards.  As the senior member of the team, provided project management guidance, database administration, and technical support.  The system was implemented using PowerBuilder on PCs running Windows 95 and Microsoft SQL Server.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description:
Provided expertise in data modeling and technical design.  During the requirements analysis phase, participated in the Joint Application Development (JAD) sessions and worked with the business analysts to identify technical issues associated with the requirements.  Worked on the deliverable for this first phase, the Business Requirements document.
Developed a logical data model using ERWin.  The model recorded relationships between business data and served as the basis for computer resource estimates and assisted the team in refining system requirements.
In the next phase of the project, the team evaluated Commercial Off the Shelf (COTS) products to use in the system design.  During this part of the project, assisted in formulating evaluation criteria, preparing the Request for Information (RFI) packet and evaluating vendor submissions.

positions.title: Consultant - System Architect
positions.description:
As a member of a three-person team, prepared a user requirements document for a Private Protective Services Board.  The board required a new system to solve Year 2000 problems and to improve existing workflows.  Analyzed the business processes, data requirements, and current computing environment.  Documented the system requirements for hardware and software with a phased implementation plan.

Served as the technical lead for a client/server application that provided support to the Private Protective Service Board.  The system tracked information on security guard licensing and authorized security firms and alarm installers in North Carolina.  The system was developed using a PowerBuilder interface using Windows NT servers and Microsoft’s SQL Server database management system.

Was responsible for gathering the requirements, developing the technical architecture, and providing technical leadership to a four-person development team during the creation and implementation of the system.  Set-up the object class libraries used during development.

positions.title: Consultant - Technical Analyst
positions.description: Was a member of a three-person team that prepared a Request for Proposal for a state government department. The RFP was for development of a system to support debt issuance and fiscal oversight responsibilities. Responsibilities included documenting staff functions and identifying current information requirements and resources.

company.name: North Carolina Department of State Treasurer

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: The system used expert system technology to monitor the output of telephone switches for faults and assisted in troubleshooting.  It was written in C, running on several different vendors’ UNIX workstations.  The system used Oracle with ProC for its database and the RTworks inference engine.  Tasks included knowledge engineering and implementing supporting functionality in C.  Defined a classification system for detection techniques and implemented tools to generate rules from simplified specifications.  Authored the C coding standards for the development team.

positions.title: Consultant - System Architect
positions.description: The purpose of the system was to automate the inventory of installed telephone switch components. The system used handheld barcode scanners and PCs.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: Participated in the design of software and firmware upgrades for a toll call data collection subsystem.  Collaborated on several system changes needed to support changes in the hardware design.  Responsibilities included providing technical guidance to team members and performing document and code reviews.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: Worked on a subsystem to integrate off-the-shelf word processing software with the existing system to perform document preparation to support Mortgage loan application processing.  The software was written in C and Object/1, and ran on PC workstations running OS/2.  The system used a Sybase database running on Sun workstations.  Tasks included design and implementation of a Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) server as a gateway between the Sybase server and the word processor.  This involved defining and coding a query language for the DDE interface and adapting an existing database interface module to run on the PC platform.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: Participated in the analysis and enhancement of tools used in the writing of telephone switching software for a telecommunications equipment manufacturer.  The software, written in C, C++ and Pascal, ran on HP workstations.  Tasks included analyzing the Motorola 68000 code produced by the Pascal compiler to identify areas of inefficiency.  Reported findings and design recommendations with supporting cost, benefit, and risk analysis.  Analyzed the impact of proposed changes in the tool set and real-time operating system.  This included estimating changes in memory requirements, recommending changes to offset increases, formulating test cases, and participating in review and validation activities.  Additionally, was responsible for implementing and testing changes in some subsystems.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: The system was designed to test digital trunks in telephone networks.  The system, implemented in C, used a Sybase database and the X Window system, and ran on Sun workstations.  Tasks included developing a GUI for UNIX user administration.  Designed and coded a report generator, and designed and implemented a subsystem for automatic periodic testing of trunks.  The system used feedback and adaptive scheduling algorithms to maximize throughput and resource utilization.  Provided software maintenance and support during system/acceptance testing and testing at customer sites.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description:
I was engaged with Bell Atlanta in Freehold, NJ as a Software Engineer on the Bell Atlanta Automated Records System (BAARS) Project.

The system automated engineering and inventory functions. Primary areas of responsibility were database design and data conversion. Development was on Sun workstations using C, the X Window System, and Sybase.  Designed and implemented a program to determine circuit routing and connectivity relationships in the telephone network.  The program used deterministic and heuristic algorithms to identify and solve problems caused by ambiguous and erroneous input data.  Designed and implemented a subsystem to parse and translate data from an existing automated system.  The rule-based system supported user extension and modification of the syntax rules.  Participated in the logical and physical database design.  The database included equipment, circuit routing and street network information.  Designed a subsystem to automate the assignment of geographic coordinates to equipment by correlating tabular data and Census Bureau TIGER files.

positions.title: Captain
positions.locationName: US Army War College, Carlisle Barracks, PA
positions.description:
Served in the roles of assistant project manager, co-designer, and lead programmer of a seven-member team that developed a major academic war-gaming model for the Department of Defense. Responsible for training, maintenance, and planning for future versions. Supported several major Department of Defense activities that used the academic war-gaming models. It replaced the TACOPS and TACLOG models (see link).
Provided the analysis, design, programming, testing, installation, training, and support for a work force accounting system used to record and analyze the workload of 350 employees. Designed and implemented many smaller classroom systems, administrative systems, and computer utilities.

Student - Teleprocessing Operations Officer Course I (TOOC)

projects.description: The Health & Alerting subsystem of the VNXe product line collates and correlates event notifications and status of other subsystems to create system status summaries and alerts for the system administrator.
